_meta.indication: PONVORY is indicated for the treatment of relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS), including clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting disease, and active secondary progressive disease, in adults.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, double-blind, 1:1 randomized, active-controlled (teriflunomide 14 mg) superiority study comparing ponesimod 20 mg daily; patients treated for 108 weeks.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with relapsing forms of MS, EDSS score of 0 to 5.5 at baseline, with at least one relapse in the year prior (or two in the prior two years).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Annualized relapse rate (ARR) over the study period, defined as confirmed relapses per subject-year.
pivotal_trials.n: 1133 patients randomized (PONVORY N=567, teriflunomide 14 mg N=566).
pivotal_trials.result: ARR 0.202 with PONVORY vs 0.290 with teriflunomide, a 30.5% relative reduction (p=0.0003); 3-month confirmed disability progression 10.8% vs 13.2% (HR 0.83, p=0.29, not significant).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence at least 10%) are upper respiratory tract infection, hepatic transaminase elevation, and hypertension. ALT elevation to at least 3x ULN occurred in 17.3% (vs 8.3% teriflunomide); bradycardia/sinus bradycardia at initiation in 5.8% (vs 1.6%); first-degree AV block in 3.4% (vs 1.2%); macular edema in 1.1% (vs none); serious or severe infections in 1.6% (vs 0.9%).
target_moa: Ponesimod is a sphingosine 1-phosphate (S1P) receptor 1 modulator that binds with high affinity to S1P receptor 1 on lymphocytes, blocking their egress from lymph nodes and reducing peripheral lymphocyte counts; the therapeutic effect in MS may involve reduced lymphocyte migration into the CNS.

rems.type: A REMS is not necessary for ponesimod.

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee meeting was held; it was not deemed necessary because the drug is not the first in its class, has a safety profile similar to the three other class members approved for this indication, acceptable trial designs, and clear efficacy findings.

basis.text: The application was reviewed under Standard (not Priority) review.

summary.text: Ponvory (ponesimod) was approved via a standard-review NDA (received 3/18/2020, PDUFA goal 3/18/2021) as a new molecular entity for relapsing forms of MS; efficacy was based on the traditional clinical endpoint of annualized relapse rate rather than accelerated approval, no advisory committee was convened, and no REMS was required.

Ponesimod (Ponvory) is a new molecular entity (NME) that is purportedly selective for S1P1, for which the Applicant (Janssen Pharmaceuticals, Inc.) has submitted a New Drug Application (NDA) with a proposed indication for the treatment of adults with RMS.
The primary endpoint was the annualized relapse rate (ARR) over the study period.
An Advisory Committee meeting was not deemed necessary for this NDA.
A REMS is not necessary for ponesimod.

requirement.text: PMR 4024-1: Deferred pediatric study — a two-part study of ponesimod in pediatric RMS patients at least 10 and less than 18 years of age (Part A open-label PK/PD dose-finding; Part B randomized non-inferiority trial with active comparator).

citations.quote: 4024-1 Conduct a two-part study of Ponvory (ponesimod) in pediatric patients with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (RMS) at least 10 years and less than 18 years of age. Part A is an open-label study of the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), and pharmacodynamics (PD) of Ponvory (ponesimod) in pediatric patients.

requirement.text: PMR 4024-2: Prospective pregnancy exposure registry cohort analyses comparing maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women with MS exposed to Ponvory during pregnancy versus two unexposed control populations.

citations.quote: 4024-2 Prospective pregnancy exposure registry cohort analyses in the United States that compare the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women with multiple sclerosis exposed to Ponvory (ponesimod) during pregnancy with two unexposed control populations: one consisting of women with multiple sclerosis who have not been exposed to Ponvory (ponesimod) before or during pregnancy and the other consisting of women without multiple sclerosis.
